methodology: Compared the Markdown and DOCX source plans for structural parity and content coverage.
Mapped registered capabilities, agents, objects, workflows, nuance classes, risks, and questions to controlled artifacts and tests.
Reviewed implementation status for duplicated foundations, unrepresented production concerns, and unresolved approval dependencies.

gaps.description: Foundational schemas and SQLite adapters exist; production database operations, migrations, backups, and tenant isolation still require deployment validation.
Film intelligence contracts and logic exist; production video ingestion, storage, annotation UI, and media QA remain to be integrated.

Legacy Play Designer assets are restored and regression-tested. A separate React and TypeScript shell, Today command center, visual Playbook library, and dedicated full-screen Play Designer authoring slice are implemented and locally validated while the Python API remains authoritative. The designer now includes an eight-step completion-aware, restartable tutorial and contextual descriptions. Film, Practice, Scouting, Game Plan, Player, Admin, and Reviews now have independent role-aware React routes with page, system, feature, workflow, status, and authority descriptions rather than legacy dashboard anchors. Advanced React parity for SSE cursors/thread resolution, version diff/merge/rollback, legality overrides, complete teaching/player workflows, multi-play export composition, and each workspace's deeper interactive controls remains, followed by full visual/accessibility/performance suites, feature-parity audit, and deployment-environment moderated pilots.

Security, rate limiting, tenant checks, signed exports, encrypted offline storage, redacted audit events, quality gates, threat-model controls, and recovery rehearsals are implemented and locally validated; production provider registration, mounted secrets, monitoring, database deployment, target-environment rollback, and operational runbook execution remain.

Controlled football bibles, authoritative rule-source registry, team-alias persistence, and synthetic team-usage validation exist; an owner-approved organization terminology bundle, full NFL lineage/team doctrine corpus, and broader real-world eval corpus remain.

redundancy_findings.finding: Multiple early foundation modules overlap with later architecture modules.
redundancy_findings.resolution: Retain early modules as compatibility foundations; treat architecture modules and controlled JSON artifacts as the authoritative expansion path.

redundancy_findings.finding: Several contract and status artifacts describe the same governance boundaries at different layers.
redundancy_findings.resolution: Keep layer-specific contracts, require shared stable IDs and eval coverage, and prohibit silent semantic divergence.

approval_dependencies: Program owner reviews this audit and the Stage 0A registry.
Program owner approves the final stage manifest and Stage 0 exit gate.
Engineering and football stakeholders validate production-scope priorities before deployment work begins.
